46	static void add_delaylist(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem,
47	                          bool asan_check)
48	{
49	#if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__)
50	  FAR struct mm_delayhead_s *delay = get_delayhead(heap);
51	  FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *tmp = mem;
52	  irqstate_t flags;
53	  bool bypass;
54	
55	  /* Delay the deallocation until a more appropriate time. */
56	
57	  flags = up_irq_save();
58	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
59	
60	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS
61	  /* Check for double-free:
62	   * Step 1: Check magic first (fast path, filters 99.99% cases)
63	   * Step 2: If magic matches, verify it's actually in delay list
64	   *         (slow path, handles extreme case where user data == magic)
65	   */
66	
67	  if (tmp->magic == ~(uintptr_t)mem)
68	    {
69	      /* Magic matches, but could be false positive from user data.
70	       * Traverse delay list to confirm this is really a duplicate.
71	       */
72	
73	      FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *node;
74	
75	      for (node = delay->head; node != NULL; node = node->flink)
76	        {
77	          if (node == tmp)
78	            {
79	              /* Confirmed: this memory is already in delay list.
80	               * This is a real double-free!
81	               */
82	
83	              kasan_bypass(bypass);
84	              up_irq_restore(flags);
85	              DEBUGASSERT(false);  /* Double-free detected! */
86	              return;
87	            }
88	        }
89	
90	      /* Magic matched but not in list - just user data coincidence.
91	       * Continue with normal flow.
92	       */
93	    }
94	
95	#  ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
96	  if (!heap->mm_mpool || !mempool_multiple_member(heap->mm_mpool, mem))
97	#  endif
98	    {
99	      FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
100	      node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)mem -
101	             MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
102	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
103	    }
104	
105	  tmp->magic = ~(uintptr_t)mem;
106	#endif
107	
108	  tmp->flink  = delay->head;
109	  delay->head = tmp;
110	
111	#if CONFIG_MM_FREE_DELAYCOUNT_MAX > 0
112	  delay->delaycount++;
113	#endif
114	
115	  if (asan_check)
116	    {
117	      size_t size = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
118	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
119	      memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, size);
120	#endif
121	      UNUSED(size);
122	      kasan_poison(mem, size);
123	    }
124	
125	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
126	  up_irq_restore(flags);
127	#endif
128	}

142	void mm_forcefree(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem)
143	{
144	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
145	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev;
146	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
147	  size_t nodesize;
148	  size_t prevsize;
149	  bool bypass;
150	
151	  /* Free mempool blk first */
152	
153	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
154	  if (heap->mm_mpool && mempool_multiple_free(heap->mm_mpool, mem) >= 0)
155	    {
156	      return;
157	    }
158	#endif
159	
160	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
161	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
162	  nodesize = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
163	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
164	  memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, nodesize);
165	#endif
166	  kasan_poison(mem, nodesize);
167	
168	  /* Map the memory chunk into a free node */
169	
170	  node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
171	         ((FAR char *)kasan_clear_tag(mem) - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
172	  nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
173	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK
174	  backtrace_remove(node->stack);
175	#endif
176	
177	  /* Sanity check against double-frees */
178	
179	  if (MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node))

182	                    mem, "double-free");

186	  node->size &= ~MM_ALLOC_BIT;
187	
188	  /* Update heap statistics */
189	
190	  heap->mm_curused -= nodesize;
191	  sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_FREE, heap, mem, nodesize, heap->mm_curused);
192	
193	  /* Check if the following node is free and, if so, merge it */
194	
195	  next = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node + nodesize);
196	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_ALLOC(next));
197	  if (MM_NODE_IS_FREE(next))
198	    {
199	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *andbeyond;
200	      size_t nextsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(next);
201	
202	      /* Get the node following the next node (which will
203	       * become the new next node). We know that we can never
204	       * index past the tail chunk because it is always allocated.
205	       */
206	
207	      andbeyond = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)((FAR char *)next + nextsize);
208	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(andbeyond) &&
209	                  andbeyond->preceding == nextsize);
210	
211	      /* Remove the next node.  There must be a predecessor,
212	       * but there may not be a successor node.
213	       */
214	
215	      DEBUGASSERT(next->blink);
216	      next->blink->flink = next->flink;
217	      if (next->flink)
218	        {
219	          next->flink->blink = next->blink;
220	        }
221	
222	      /* Then merge the two chunks */
223	
224	      nodesize            += nextsize;
225	      node->size           = nodesize | (node->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
226	      andbeyond->preceding = nodesize;
227	      next                 = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)andbeyond;
228	    }
229	  else
230	    {
231	      next->size     |= MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
232	      next->preceding = nodesize;
233	    }
234	
235	  /* Check if the preceding node is also free and, if so, merge
236	   * it with this node

238	
239	  if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
240	    {
241	      prev = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
242	        ((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
243	      prevsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
244	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_FREE(prev) && node->preceding == prevsize);

246	      /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
247	       * not be a successor node.

250	      DEBUGASSERT(prev->blink);
251	      prev->blink->flink = prev->flink;

695	 *
696	 * Description:
697	 *   Try to receive packets from device and pass packets into IP
698	 *   stack and send packets which is from IP stack if necessary.
699	 *
700	 * Input Parameters:
701	 *   upper - Reference to the upper half driver structure
702	 *
703	 * Assumptions:
704	 *   Called with the network locked.
705	 *
706	 ****************************************************************************/
707	
708	static void netdev_upper_rxpoll_work(FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper)
709	{
710	  FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
711	  FAR struct net_driver_s       *dev   = &lower->netdev;
712	  FAR netpkt_t                  *pkt;
713	
714	  /* Loop while receive() successfully retrieves valid Ethernet frames. */
715	
716	  netdev_lock(dev);
717	  while ((pkt = lower->ops->receive(lower)) != NULL)
718	    {
719	      if (!IFF_IS_UP(dev->d_flags))
720	        {
721	          /* Interface down, drop frame */
722	
723	          NETDEV_RXDROPPED(dev);
724	          netpkt_free(lower, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
725	          nerr("ERROR: Dropped frame due to lower dev not up\n");
726	          continue;
727	        }
728	
729	      netpkt_put(dev, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
730	      NETDEV_RXPACKETS(dev);
731	
732	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
733	      /* When packet sockets are enabled, feed the frame into the tap */
734	
735	      pkt_input(dev);
736	#endif
737	
738	      switch (dev->d_lltype)
739	        {
740	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK
741	        case NET_LL_LOOPBACK:
742	#endif
743	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET
744	        case NET_LL_ETHERNET:
745	#endif
746	#ifdef CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211
747	        case NET_LL_IEEE80211:
748	#endif
749	#if defined(CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK) || defined(CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET) || \
750	    defined(CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211)
751	          eth_input(dev);
752	          break;
753	#endif
754	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_MBIM
755	        case NET_LL_MBIM:
756	          ip_input(dev);
757	          break;
758	#endif
759	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_CAN
760	        case NET_LL_CAN:
761	          ninfo("CAN frame");
762	          can_input(dev);
763	          break;
764	#endif
765	        default:
766	          nerr("Unknown link type %d\n", dev->d_lltype);
767	          break;
768	        }
769	    }
770	
771	  netdev_unlock(dev);
772	}

99	 * Private Functions — Reset and Clock Control
100	 ****************************************************************************/
101	
102	static void reset_assert(unsigned int id)
103	{
104	  unsigned int bank = id / 32;
105	  unsigned int bit  = id % 32;
106	  uint32_t reg;
107	
108	  reg = getreg32(REG_RESET_BANK(bank));
109	  putreg32(reg & ~(1u << bit), REG_RESET_BANK(bank));
110	}
111	
112	static void reset_deassert(unsigned int id)
113	{
114	  unsigned int bank = id / 32;
115	  unsigned int bit  = id % 32;
116	  uint32_t reg;
117	
118	  reg = getreg32(REG_RESET_BANK(bank));
119	  putreg32(reg | (1u << bit), REG_RESET_BANK(bank));
120	}
121	
122	static void clk_reset_deassert(unsigned int id)
123	{
124	  unsigned int bank = id / 32;
125	  unsigned int bit  = id % 32;
126	  uintptr_t addr = SG2000_CLKGEN_BASE + bank * 4;
127	  uint32_t reg;
128	
129	  reg = getreg32(addr);
130	  putreg32(reg | (1u << bit), addr);
131	}

133	/****************************************************************************
134	 * Private Functions — Clock Enable
135	 *
136	 * Enables the GMAC 500MHz and AXI4 clocks, deasserts resets.
137	 * Reference: Manual §10.3 Phase 1.1
138	 ****************************************************************************/
139	
140	static void gmac_clock_enable(void)
141	{
142	  uint32_t reg;
143	
144	  /* Enable GMAC0 clocks: clk_500m_eth0 + clk_axi4_eth0 */
145	
146	  reg = getreg32(REG_CLK_EN_0);
147	  reg |= CLK_EN_ETH0_500M | CLK_EN_ETH0_AXI4;
148	  putreg32(reg, REG_CLK_EN_0);
149	
150	  /* Deassert clock-domain resets in the clkgen controller */
151	
152	  clk_reset_deassert(CLK_RST_500M_ETH0);
153	  clk_reset_deassert(CLK_RST_AXI_ETH0);
154	
155	  /* Release the main reset-controller lines for GMAC and built-in EPHY */
156	
157	  reset_assert(RST_ETH0);
158	  reset_assert(RST_ETHPHY);
159	  reset_assert(RST_ETHPHYRST_APB);
160	  up_udelay(10);
161	  reset_deassert(RST_ETHPHYRST_APB);
162	  reset_deassert(RST_ETHPHY);
163	  reset_deassert(RST_ETH0);
164	  up_udelay(10);
165	
166	  ethinfo("GMAC clocks enabled, CLK_EN_0=0x%08" PRIX32
167	          " RESET0=0x%08" PRIX32 " RESET3=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
168	          getreg32(REG_CLK_EN_0), getreg32(REG_RESET_BANK(0)),
169	          getreg32(REG_RESET_BANK(3)));
170	}

172	/****************************************************************************
173	 * Private Functions — D-Cache Operations (T-Head C906)
174	 *
175	 * The C906 has a 32KB 4-way set-associative D-Cache with 64-byte cache
176	 * lines using PIPT (Physical Index + Physical Tag).  DDR memory
177	 * (0x80000000-0xC0000000) is mapped as cacheable.  DMA descriptors and
178	 * buffers allocated from the kernel heap are therefore cacheable, and
179	 * explicit cache maintenance is REQUIRED before any DMA engine access.
180	 *
181	 * The Synopsys DWMAC1000 DMA engine is NOT cache-coherent on this SoC.
182	 *
183	 * T-Head custom instructions (from CV181x/SG2002 TRM):
184	 *   dcache.cpa  rs1  (0x0295000b)  – Clean (write back) by physical addr
185	 *   dcache.ipa  rs1  (0x02a5000b)  – Invalidate by physical addr
186	 *   dcache.cipa rs1  (0x02b5000b)  – Clean + Invalidate by physical addr
187	 *   sync.s           (0x01b0000b)  – Cache operation sync barrier
188	 ****************************************************************************/
189	
190	static void dcache_clean_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
191	{
192	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
193	
194	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
195	    {
196	      asm volatile (".long 0x0295000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.cpa a0 */
197	    }
198	
199	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
200	}
201	
202	static void dcache_invalidate_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
203	{
204	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
205	
206	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
207	    {
208	      asm volatile (".long 0x02a5000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.ipa a0 */
209	    }
210	
211	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
212	}
213	
214	static void dcache_flush_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
215	{
216	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
217	
218	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
219	    {
220	      asm volatile (".long 0x02b5000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.cipa a0 */
221	    }
222	
223	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
224	}

226	/****************************************************************************
227	 * Private Functions — DMA Software Reset
228	 *
229	 * Reference: Manual §4.4 Step 1, §10.3 Phase 2.1
230	 ****************************************************************************/
231	
232	static int dma_soft_reset(uintptr_t gmac_base)
233	{
234	  uint32_t val;
235	  int timeout;
236	
237	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE);
238	  putreg32(val | DMA_SFT_RESET, gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE);
239	
240	  timeout = (DMA_RESET_TIMEOUT_MS * 1000) / 10;  /* 10us per iteration */
241	  do
242	    {
243	      val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE);
244	      if (!(val & DMA_SFT_RESET))
245	        {
246	          return OK;
247	        }
248	
249	      up_udelay(10);
250	    }
251	  while (--timeout > 0);
252	
253	  etherr("DMA reset timeout bus_mode=0x%08" PRIX32 " hw_feature=0x%08"
254	         PRIX32 "\n",
255	         getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE),
256	         getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_HW_FEATURE));
257	  return -ETIMEDOUT;
258	}

425	/****************************************************************************
426	 * Name: ephy_hardware_reset
427	 *
428	 * Description:
429	 *   Minimal EPHY init: release resets, set PHY ID, switch to MDIO control.
430	 *   Matches Linux bm_eth_reset_phy() in dwmac-cvitek.c.
431	 *   Does NOT run the full analog tuning sequence — that is done after
432	 *   MDIO is confirmed operational.
433	 *
434	 * Reference: Manual §2.8, §10.3 Phase 1.2
435	 ****************************************************************************/
436	
437	static void ephy_hardware_reset(uintptr_t phy_base, uintptr_t phy_top)
438	{
439	  ephy_led_pinmux();
440	
441	  /* Select APB interface to access EPHY registers */
442	
443	  putreg32(0x0001, phy_top + 0x4);
444	
445	  /* Release shutdown */
446	
447	  putreg32(0x0900, phy_top);
448	
449	  /* Release dig_rst_n — enables MII register access via APB */
450	
451	  putreg32(0x0904, phy_top);
452	
453	  /* Switch to Page 5 for ANA initialization */
454	
455	  putreg32(0x0500, phy_base + 0x7c);
456	
457	  /* ANA_PD (power-down release) */
458	
459	  putreg32(0x0c00, phy_base + 0x40);
460	
461	  /* ANA_EN */
462	
463	  putreg32(0x0c7e, phy_base + 0x40);
464	  up_mdelay(1);
465	
466	  /* Release ana_rst_n */
467	
468	  putreg32(0x0906, phy_top);
469	  putreg32(0x0500, phy_base + 0x7c);
470	
471	  /* Program PHY ID into EPHY registers (so MDIO can discover it) */
472	
473	  putreg32(0x0043, phy_base + 0x08);  /* PHY_ID_HIGH */
474	  putreg32(0x5649, phy_base + 0x0c);  /* PHY_ID_LOW */
475	
476	  ethinfo("EPHY APB PHYID=0x%04" PRIX32 "%04" PRIX32 "\n",
477	          getreg32(phy_base + 0x08) & 0xffff,
478	          getreg32(phy_base + 0x0c) & 0xffff);
479	
480	  /* Switch control to MDIO (GMAC) so the DWMAC1000 MDIO controller can
481	   * discover and communicate with the PHY.
482	   */
483	
484	  putreg32(0x0000, phy_top + 0x4);
485	  up_mdelay(10);
486	
487	  ethinfo("EPHY init done top=0x%08" PRIX32 " sel=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
488	          getreg32(phy_top), getreg32(phy_top + 0x4));
489	}

522	/****************************************************************************
523	 * Private Functions — MDIO (MII Management Interface)
524	 *
525	 * CV181x uses the TRM Chapter 18 legacy GMAC MDIO layout at offsets
526	 * 0x10/0x14.  The standard DWMAC4 MDIO controller at 0x200/0x204 is
527	 * NOT functional on this silicon.
528	 *
529	 * Reference: Manual §8.2, §8.3, §10.10
530	 ****************************************************************************/
531	
532	static int mdio_wait_ready(uintptr_t gmac_base)
533	{
534	  int timeout = 10000;
535	
536	  do
537	    {
538	      if (!(getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_MII_ADDR) & GMAC_MII_ADDR_BUSY))
539	        {
540	          return OK;
541	        }
542	
543	      up_udelay(1);
544	    }
545	  while (--timeout > 0);
546	
547	  return -ETIMEDOUT;
548	}
549	
550	static uint16_t mdio_read(uintptr_t gmac_base, uint8_t phy_addr,
551	                          uint8_t reg_addr)
552	{
553	  uint32_t cmd;
554	
555	  if (mdio_wait_ready(gmac_base) < 0)
556	    {
557	      return 0xffff;
558	    }
559	
560	  putreg32(0, gmac_base + GMAC_MII_DATA);
561	
562	  cmd = (((uint32_t)phy_addr & 0x1f) << GMAC_MII_ADDR_PHY_SHIFT) |
563	        (((uint32_t)reg_addr & 0x1f) << GMAC_MII_ADDR_REG_SHIFT) |
564	        GMAC_MII_ADDR_CR_250_300M | GMAC_MII_ADDR_BUSY;
565	
566	  putreg32(cmd, gmac_base + GMAC_MII_ADDR);
567	
568	  if (mdio_wait_ready(gmac_base) < 0)
569	    {
570	      return 0xffff;
571	    }
572	
573	  return (uint16_t)(getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_MII_DATA) & 0xffff);
574	}
575	
576	static void mdio_write(uintptr_t gmac_base, uint8_t phy_addr,
577	                       uint8_t reg_addr, uint16_t data)
578	{
579	  uint32_t cmd;
580	
581	  if (mdio_wait_ready(gmac_base) < 0)
582	    {
583	      return;
584	    }
585	
586	  putreg32(data, gmac_base + GMAC_MII_DATA);
587	
588	  cmd = (((uint32_t)phy_addr & 0x1f) << GMAC_MII_ADDR_PHY_SHIFT) |
589	        (((uint32_t)reg_addr & 0x1f) << GMAC_MII_ADDR_REG_SHIFT) |
590	        GMAC_MII_ADDR_CR_250_300M | GMAC_MII_ADDR_WRITE | GMAC_MII_ADDR_BUSY;
591	
592	  putreg32(cmd, gmac_base + GMAC_MII_ADDR);
593	  mdio_wait_ready(gmac_base);
594	}

596	/****************************************************************************
597	 * Name: mdio_verify_phy
598	 *
599	 * Description:
600	 *   Read PHY ID via MDIO to verify the PHY is accessible.
601	 *
602	 * Reference: Manual §10.3
603	 ****************************************************************************/
604	
605	static int mdio_verify_phy(uintptr_t gmac_base)
606	{
607	  uint16_t id1;
608	  uint16_t id2;
609	  uint32_t phy_id;
610	
611	  id1 = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 2);  /* PHY ID 1 register */
612	  id2 = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 3);  /* PHY ID 2 register */
613	  phy_id = ((uint32_t)id1 << 16) | id2;
614	
615	  ethinfo("MDIO PHY ID=0x%08" PRIX32 " (expected 0x%08" PRIX32 ")\n",
616	          phy_id, (uint32_t)CVITEK_PHY_ID);
617	
618	  if (id1 == 0xffff || id2 == 0xffff)
619	    {
620	      etherr("MDIO timeout reading PHY ID\n");
621	      return -ENODEV;
622	    }
623	
624	  if (phy_id != CVITEK_PHY_ID)
625	    {
626	      ethwarn("Unexpected PHY ID 0x%08" PRIX32 " (expected 0x%08"
627	              PRIX32 ")\n", phy_id, (uint32_t)CVITEK_PHY_ID);
628	    }
629	
630	  return OK;
631	}

633	/****************************************************************************
634	 * Private Functions — PHY Configuration (Auto-Negotiation)
635	 *
636	 * Resets the PHY, starts auto-negotiation, waits for link, and reads
637	 * the negotiated speed and duplex mode.
638	 *
639	 * Reference: Manual §10.3 (part of Phase 7)
640	 ****************************************************************************/
641	
642	static int phy_config_init(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv)
643	{
644	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
645	  uint16_t bmsr;
646	  uint16_t bmcr;
647	  uint16_t anlpar;
648	  int timeout;
649	
650	  /* Reset PHY */
651	
652	  mdio_write(gmac_base, 0, 0, 0x8000);  /* BMCR reset */
653	  timeout = (PHY_RESET_TIMEOUT_MS * 1000) / 1000;
654	  do
655	    {
656	      up_mdelay(1);
657	      bmcr = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 0);
658	      if (!(bmcr & 0x8000))
659	        {
660	          break;
661	        }
662	    }
663	  while (--timeout > 0);
664	
665	  ethinfo("PHY reset done, BMCR=0x%04" PRIX16 "\n", bmcr);
666	
667	  /* Advertise capabilities: 100BASE-TX full/half, 10BASE-T full/half */
668	
669	  mdio_write(gmac_base, 0, 4, 0x01e1);
670	
671	  /* Start auto-negotiation */
672	
673	  bmcr = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 0);
674	  mdio_write(gmac_base, 0, 0, bmcr | 0x1200);  /* AN enable + restart AN */
675	  ethinfo("Autoneg start, BMCR=0x%04" PRIX16 "\n", bmcr | 0x1200);
676	
677	  /* Wait for link up */
678	
679	  timeout = PHY_AN_TIMEOUT_MS / 100;
680	  do
681	    {
682	      up_mdelay(100);
683	      bmsr = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 1);
684	      if (bmsr & 0x0004)  /* Link Status bit */
685	        {
686	          break;
687	        }
688	    }
689	  while (--timeout > 0);
690	
691	  if (!(bmsr & 0x0004))
692	    {
693	      ethwarn("PHY link down, BMSR=0x%04" PRIX16 "\n", bmsr);
694	      priv->link_up = 0;
695	      return OK;
696	    }
697	
698	  /* Read negotiated speed/duplex from Link Partner Ability */
699	
700	  anlpar = mdio_read(gmac_base, 0, 5);
701	  ethinfo("PHY link up, BMSR=0x%04" PRIX16 " ANLPAR=0x%04" PRIX16 "\n",
702	          bmsr, anlpar);
703	
704	  /* Determine speed and duplex from auto-negotiation result */
705	
706	  if (anlpar & 0x0100)          /* 100BASE-TX Full Duplex */
707	    {
708	      priv->speed  = 100;
709	      priv->duplex = 1;
710	    }
711	  else if (anlpar & 0x0080)     /* 100BASE-TX Half Duplex */
712	    {
713	      priv->speed  = 100;
714	      priv->duplex = 0;
715	    }
716	  else if (anlpar & 0x0040)     /* 10BASE-T Full Duplex */
717	    {
718	      priv->speed  = 10;
719	      priv->duplex = 1;
720	    }
721	  else                          /* 10BASE-T Half Duplex (default) */
722	    {
723	      priv->speed  = 10;
724	      priv->duplex = 0;
725	    }
726	
727	  priv->link_up = 1;
728	
729	  ethinfo("Negotiated: %d Mbps %s duplex\n",
730	          priv->speed, priv->duplex ? "Full" : "Half");
731	
732	  return OK;
733	}

735	/****************************************************************************
736	 * Private Functions — DMA Descriptor Allocation
737	 *
738	 * Allocates TX and RX descriptor rings and RX data buffers.
739	 * All memory is 64-byte aligned for C906 D-Cache line isolation.
740	 *
741	 * Reference: Manual §10.3 Phase 3, §10.7
742	 ****************************************************************************/
743	
744	static int alloc_dma(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv)
745	{
746	  unsigned int i;
747	  size_t tx_desc_sz;
748	  size_t rx_desc_sz;
749	
750	  if (priv->dma_allocated)
751	    {
752	      return OK;
753	    }
754	
755	  tx_desc_sz = TX_RING_SIZE * sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s);
756	  rx_desc_sz = RX_RING_SIZE * sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s);
757	
758	  /* Allocate descriptor rings with cache-line alignment */
759	
760	  priv->tx_desc = (struct sg2000_dma_desc_s *)
761	    kmm_memalign(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, tx_desc_sz);
762	  priv->rx_desc = (struct sg2000_dma_desc_s *)
763	    kmm_memalign(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, rx_desc_sz);
764	
765	  if (!priv->tx_desc || !priv->rx_desc)
766	    {
767	      etherr("Failed to allocate DMA descriptor rings\n");
768	      return -ENOMEM;
769	    }
770	
771	  memset(priv->tx_desc, 0, tx_desc_sz);
772	  memset(priv->rx_desc, 0, rx_desc_sz);
773	
774	  /* For identity-mapped builds, virtual = physical */
775	
776	  priv->tx_desc_phys = (uintptr_t)priv->tx_desc;
777	  priv->rx_desc_phys = (uintptr_t)priv->rx_desc;
778	
779	  /* Allocate TX data buffers */
780	
781	  for (i = 0; i < TX_RING_SIZE; i++)
782	    {
783	      priv->tx_buf[i] = (uint8_t *)
784	        kmm_memalign(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, TX_BUF_SIZE);
785	      if (!priv->tx_buf[i])
786	        {
787	          etherr("Failed to allocate TX buffer %u\n", i);
788	          return -ENOMEM;
789	        }
790	
791	      priv->tx_buf_phys[i] = (uintptr_t)priv->tx_buf[i];
792	      priv->tx_pkt[i] = NULL;
793	    }
794	
795	  /* Allocate RX data buffers */
796	
797	  for (i = 0; i < RX_RING_SIZE; i++)
798	    {
799	      priv->rx_buf[i] = (uint8_t *)
800	        kmm_memalign(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, RX_BUF_SIZE);
801	      if (!priv->rx_buf[i])
802	        {
803	          etherr("Failed to allocate RX buffer %u\n", i);
804	          return -ENOMEM;
805	        }
806	
807	      priv->rx_buf_phys[i] = (uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[i];
808	    }
809	
810	  priv->dma_allocated = true;
811	
812	  ethinfo("DMA memory allocated: TX ring %u descs, RX ring %u descs\n",
813	          (unsigned int)TX_RING_SIZE, (unsigned int)RX_RING_SIZE);
814	
815	  return OK;
816	}
817	
818	/****************************************************************************
819	 * Private Functions — Descriptor Ring Initialization
820	 *
821	 * Reference: Manual §3.5, §10.3 Phase 4
822	 ****************************************************************************/
823	
824	static void init_desc_rings(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv)
825	{
826	  unsigned int i;
827	  unsigned int last_rx = RX_RING_SIZE - 1;
828	
829	  /* Initialize TX descriptors: OWN=0 (CPU owns all).
830	   * CV181x Ring Mode convention: END_RING=1 on ALL TX descriptors.
831	   * DMA uses DMA_TX_BASE_ADDR + ring length for wrapping, not END_RING.
832	   * For basic descriptors (ATDS=0), END_RING is in TDES1 bit 25.
833	   */
834	
835	  for (i = 0; i < TX_RING_SIZE; i++)
836	    {
837	      priv->tx_desc[i].des0 = 0;
838	      priv->tx_desc[i].des1 = (i == (TX_RING_SIZE - 1)) ? TDES1_END_RING : 0;
839	      priv->tx_desc[i].des2 = priv->tx_buf_phys[i];
840	      priv->tx_desc[i].des3 = 0;
841	      priv->tx_pkt[i] = NULL;
842	    }
843	    priv->tx_desc[TX_RING_SIZE - 1].des3 = &priv->tx_desc[0];  /* Ring wrap pointer */
844	
845	  /* Flush TX descriptor ring so DMA sees initialized state */
846	
847	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)priv->tx_desc,
848	                     (uintptr_t)(priv->tx_desc + TX_RING_SIZE));
849	
850	  /* Initialize RX descriptors: OWN=1 (DMA owns all), END_RING on last.
851	   * For basic descriptors (ATDS=0), END_RING is in RDES1 bit 25.
852	   */
853	
854	  for (i = 0; i < RX_RING_SIZE; i++)
855	    {
856	      priv->rx_desc[i].des0 = RDES0_OWN;
857	      priv->rx_desc[i].des1 = (RX_BUF_SIZE & RDES1_BUFFER1_SIZE_MASK) |
858	                              ((i == last_rx) ? RDES1_END_RING : 0);
859	      priv->rx_desc[i].des2 = priv->rx_buf_phys[i];
860	      priv->rx_desc[i].des3 = 0;
861	    }
862	    priv->rx_desc[last_rx].des3 = &priv->rx_desc[0];  /* Ring wrap pointer */
863	
864	  /* Flush RX descriptor ring and data buffers before DMA touches them */
865	
866	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)priv->rx_desc,
867	                     (uintptr_t)(priv->rx_desc + RX_RING_SIZE));
868	
869	  for (i = 0; i < RX_RING_SIZE; i++)
870	    {
871	      dcache_flush_range((uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[i],
872	                         (uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[i] + RX_BUF_SIZE);
873	    }
874	
875	  /* Reset ring indices */
876	
877	  priv->tx_cur   = 0;
878	  priv->tx_dirty = 0;
879	  priv->rx_cur   = 0;
880	
881	  ethinfo("Descriptor rings initialized\n");
882	}

884	/****************************************************************************
885	 * Private Functions — MAC Address Configuration
886	 *
887	 * Reference: Manual §4.4 Step 6, §10.3 Phase 5.3
888	 ****************************************************************************/
889	
890	static void set_mac_addr(uintptr_t gmac_base, const uint8_t *mac)
891	{
892	  uint32_t hi;
893	  uint32_t lo;
894	
895	  hi = ((uint32_t)mac[5] << 8) | (uint32_t)mac[4] | GMAC_HI_REG_AE;
896	  lo = ((uint32_t)mac[3] << 24) | ((uint32_t)mac[2] << 16) |
897	       ((uint32_t)mac[1] << 8)  | (uint32_t)mac[0];
898	
899	  putreg32(hi, gmac_base + GMAC_MAC_ADDR0_HIGH);
900	  putreg32(lo, gmac_base + GMAC_MAC_ADDR0_LOW);
901	
902	  ethinfo("MAC addr set: %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x\n",
903	          mac[0], mac[1], mac[2], mac[3], mac[4], mac[5]);
904	}

906	/****************************************************************************
907	 * Private Functions — MAC Core and DMA Initialization
908	 *
909	 * Performs the full hardware initialization sequence:
910	 *   - DMA bus mode and AXI configuration
911	 *   - MAC core init (GMAC_CONTROL, interrupt mask, frame filter)
912	 *   - DMA operation mode (Store-and-Forward)
913	 *   - Interrupt enable
914	 *   - Write descriptor base addresses
915	 *   - Start DMA TX and RX
916	 *
917	 * Reference: Manual §10.3 Phase 2, 5, 6, 7
918	 ****************************************************************************/
919	
920	static int hw_setup(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv)
921	{
922	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
923	  uint32_t val;
924	
925	  /* --- Phase 2: DMA software reset --- */
926	
927	  if (dma_soft_reset(gmac_base) < 0)
928	    {
929	      return -ETIMEDOUT;
930	    }
931	
932	  /* --- Phase 2.2: Configure DMA Bus Mode ---
933	   * PBL=8, RPBL=8, FB=1 (fixed burst), USP=1 (separate PBL),
934	   * AAL=1 (address-aligned beats).  ATDS is NOT set (basic descriptors).
935	   * Use explicit constants; (DMA_PBL_8 & 0x3f) would be 0 (PBL field is
936	   * at bits 8-13, masking with 0x3f gives 0).
937	   */
938	
939	  val = DMA_PBL_8 | ((3 << DMA_RPBL_SHIFT) & DMA_RPBL_MASK) |
940	        DMA_FB | DMA_USP | DMA_AAL;
941	  putreg32(val, gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE);
942	
943	  /* --- Phase 2.3: Configure AXI bus ---
944	   * WR_OSR_LMT=1, RD_OSR_LMT=2, BLEN support for 4/8/16 beats.
945	   */
946	
947	  putreg32((1 << DMA_AXI_WR_OSR_LMT_SHIFT) |
948	           (2 << DMA_AXI_RD_OSR_LMT_SHIFT) |
949	           (0xf << DMA_AXI_BLEN_SHIFT),
950	           gmac_base + DMA_AXI_BUS_MODE);
951	
952	  ethinfo("DMA: bus_mode=0x%08" PRIX32 " axi=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
953	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE),
954	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_AXI_BUS_MODE));
955	
956	  /* --- Phase 5.1: Configure GMAC_CONTROL ---
957	   * Use read-modify-write to preserve speed/duplex (FES, DM) already
958	   * set by gmac_set_speed_duplex() before hw_setup() was called.
959	   */
960	
961	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
962	  putreg32(val | GMAC_CORE_INIT, gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
963	
964	  /* --- Phase 5.2: Configure GMAC_INT_MASK (disable all MAC interrupts,
965	   *   use DMA interrupts only) ---
966	   */
967	
968	  putreg32(GMAC_INT_DEFAULT_MASK, gmac_base + GMAC_INT_MASK);
969	
970	  /* --- Phase 5.4: Configure frame filter ---
971	   * Use promiscuous mode (PR) to accept all packets.  This matches the
972	   * old driver's setup and avoids MAC address filtering issues.
973	   */
974	
975	  putreg32(GMAC_FILTER_PR | GMAC_FILTER_HMC | GMAC_FILTER_PM,
976	           gmac_base + GMAC_FRAME_FILTER);
977	
978	  /* Clear VLAN tag */
979	
980	  putreg32(0, gmac_base + GMAC_VLAN_TAG);
981	
982	  /* Clear pending MAC and DMA interrupts */
983	
984	  putreg32(0xffffffff, gmac_base + GMAC_INT_STATUS);
985	  putreg32(DMA_STATUS_W1C_MASK, gmac_base + DMA_STATUS);
986	
987	  /* --- Phase 5.5: Enable MAC TX and RX --- */
988	
989	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
990	  putreg32(val | GMAC_CONTROL_TE | GMAC_CONTROL_RE, gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
991	
992	  /* --- Phase 6.1: Configure DMA operation mode ---
993	   * RSF=1 (RX Store-and-Forward), TSF=1 (TX Store-and-Forward),
994	   * OSF=1 (Operate on Second Frame), RTC=64, TTC=64.
995	   */
996	
997	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
998	  val |= DMA_CONTROL_RSF | DMA_CONTROL_TSF | DMA_CONTROL_OSF |
999	         DMA_CONTROL_RTC_64 | DMA_CONTROL_TTC_64;
1000	  putreg32(val, gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1001	
1002	  /* --- Phase 6.2: Enable DMA interrupts --- */
1003	
1004	  putreg32(DMA_INTR_DEFAULT_MASK, gmac_base + DMA_INTR_ENA);
1005	
1006	  /* --- Phase 7.1: Write descriptor base addresses --- */
1007	
1008	  putreg32(priv->tx_desc_phys, gmac_base + DMA_TX_BASE_ADDR);
1009	  putreg32(priv->rx_desc_phys, gmac_base + DMA_RCV_BASE_ADDR);
1010	
1011	  /* --- Phase 7.2-7.3: Start DMA TX and RX ---
1012	   * Write ST first, then SR separately with a delay.  The hardware
1013	   * may ignore SR if written simultaneously with ST.
1014	   */
1015	
1016	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1017	  putreg32(val | DMA_CONTROL_ST, gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1018	  up_udelay(10);
1019	
1020	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1021	  putreg32(val | DMA_CONTROL_SR, gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1022	  up_udelay(10);
1023	
1024	  ethinfo("MAC/DMA started: gmac_ctrl=0x%08" PRIX32
1025	          " dma_ctrl=0x%08" PRIX32 " dma_status=0x%08" PRIX32
1026	          " dma_intr=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
1027	          getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL),
1028	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL),
1029	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_STATUS),
1030	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_INTR_ENA));
1031	
1032	  return OK;
1033	}

1035	/****************************************************************************
1036	 * Name: gmac_set_speed_duplex
1037	 *
1038	 * Description:
1039	 *   Configure GMAC speed and duplex mode based on PHY negotiation result.
1040	 *
1041	 * Reference: Manual §10.9
1042	 ****************************************************************************/
1043	
1044	static void gmac_set_speed_duplex(uintptr_t gmac_base, int speed, int duplex)
1045	{
1046	  uint32_t val;
1047	
1048	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
1049	
1050	  /* Clear speed and duplex bits */
1051	
1052	  val &= ~(GMAC_CONTROL_FES | GMAC_CONTROL_DM);
1053	
1054	  /* Set speed: FES=1 for 100Mbps, FES=0 for 10Mbps */
1055	
1056	  if (speed == 100)
1057	    {
1058	      val |= GMAC_CONTROL_FES;
1059	    }
1060	
1061	  /* Set duplex: DM=1 for full duplex */
1062	
1063	  if (duplex)
1064	    {
1065	      val |= GMAC_CONTROL_DM;
1066	    }
1067	
1068	  putreg32(val, gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
1069	}

1071	/****************************************************************************
1072	 * Private Functions — DMA Doorbell
1073	 *
1074	 * Writing any value to DMA_XMT_POLL_DEMAND / DMA_RCV_POLL_DEMAND
1075	 * triggers the DMA engine to re-fetch descriptors from the ring.
1076	 *
1077	 * Reference: Manual §2.3, §10.4, §10.5
1078	 ****************************************************************************/
1079	
1080	static void tx_doorbell(uintptr_t gmac_base)
1081	{
1082	  putreg32(0, gmac_base + DMA_XMT_POLL_DEMAND);
1083	}
1084	
1085	static void rx_doorbell(uintptr_t gmac_base)
1086	{
1087	  putreg32(0, gmac_base + DMA_RCV_POLL_DEMAND);
1088	}
1089	
1090	/****************************************************************************
1091	 * Private Functions — Hardware Transmit
1092	 *
1093	 * Prepares a TX descriptor, copies data to the DMA buffer, and signals
1094	 * the DMA engine to transmit.
1095	 *
1096	 * Reference: Manual §5.2, §10.4
1097	 ****************************************************************************/
1098	
1099	static int hw_transmit(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv,
1100	                       const uint8_t *data, unsigned int len)
1101	{
1102	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
1103	  unsigned int idx = priv->tx_cur;
1104	  struct sg2000_dma_desc_s *desc = &priv->tx_desc[idx];
1105	  irqstate_t flags;
1106	
1107	  /* Check if ring is full */
1108	
1109	  if (desc->des0 & TDES0_OWN)
1110	    {
1111	      return -EBUSY;
1112	    }
1113	
1114	  /* Copy data to pre-allocated TX DMA buffer */
1115	
1116	  memcpy(priv->tx_buf[idx], data, len);
1117	
1118	  /* Write back TX buffer so DMA can see packet data */
1119	
1120	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)priv->tx_buf[idx],
1121	                     (uintptr_t)priv->tx_buf[idx] + len);
1122	
1123	  /* Fill descriptor (basic format, 16 bytes):
1124	   *   des0: OWN + IC
1125	   *   des1: buffer size + FS + LS + END_RING + IC
1126	   *   des2: buffer physical address
1127	   */
1128	
1129	  desc->des2 = priv->tx_buf_phys[idx];
1130	  desc->des1 = (len & TDES1_BUFFER1_SIZE_MASK) |
1131	               TDES1_FIRST_SEGMENT | TDES1_LAST_SEGMENT |
1132	               ((idx == (TX_RING_SIZE - 1)) ? TDES1_END_RING : 0) |
1133	               TDES1_INTERRUPT;
1134	
1135	  /* Memory barrier: ensure descriptor writes are visible to DMA
1136	   * before setting OWN=1.
1137	   */
1138	
1139	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1140	                     (uintptr_t)desc + sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1141	  __asm__ volatile ("fence w,w" ::: "memory");
1142	
1143	  /* Give ownership to DMA.  IC and END_RING are set in des1 above. */
1144	
1145	  desc->des0 = TDES0_OWN;
1146	
1147	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1148	                     (uintptr_t)desc + sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1149	
1150	  /* Advance TX pointer and ring doorbell */
1151	
1152	  flags = up_irq_save();
1153	  priv->tx_cur = (idx + 1) & (TX_RING_SIZE - 1);
1154	  tx_doorbell(gmac_base);
1155	  up_irq_restore(flags);
1156	
1157	  ethinfo("TX: %u bytes desc[%u] des0=0x%08" PRIX32
1158	          " des1=0x%08" PRIX32 " des2=0x%08" PRIX32
1159	          " dma_status=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
1160	          len, idx, desc->des0, desc->des1, desc->des2,
1161	          getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_STATUS));
1162	
1163	  return OK;
1164	}
1165	
1166	/****************************************************************************
1167	 * Private Functions — TX Cleanup
1168	 *
1169	 * Frees completed TX packets by walking from dirty_tx to cur_tx.
1170	 * Called from ISR on TX Complete interrupt.
1171	 *
1172	 * Reference: Manual §5.3, §10.4 step 7
1173	 ****************************************************************************/
1174	
1175	static void tx_cleanup(struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv)
1176	{
1177	  irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
1178	
1179	  while (priv->tx_dirty != priv->tx_cur)
1180	    {
1181	      struct sg2000_dma_desc_s *desc = &priv->tx_desc[priv->tx_dirty];
1182	
1183	      /* Invalidate descriptor cache line to read DMA-written status */
1184	
1185	      dcache_invalidate_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1186	                              (uintptr_t)desc +
1187	                              sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1188	
1189	      if (desc->des0 & TDES0_OWN)
1190	        {
1191	          break;  /* Still owned by DMA */
1192	        }
1193	
1194	      /* Check for TX errors */
1195	
1196	      if (desc->des0 & TDES0_ERROR_SUMMARY)
1197	        {
1198	          etherr("TX error desc[%u] status=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
1199	                 priv->tx_dirty, desc->des0);
1200	        }
1201	
1202	      /* Free the tracked netpkt and notify upper half */
1203	
1204	      if (priv->tx_pkt[priv->tx_dirty] != NULL)
1205	        {
1206	          netpkt_free(&priv->dev, priv->tx_pkt[priv->tx_dirty], NETPKT_TX);
1207	          priv->tx_pkt[priv->tx_dirty] = NULL;
1208	          netdev_lower_txdone(&priv->dev);
1209	        }
1210	
1211	      /* Clear descriptor for reuse, END_RING=1 on all (CV181x convention) */
1212	
1213	      desc->des0 = 0;
1214	      desc->des1 = (priv->tx_dirty == (TX_RING_SIZE - 1)) ?
1215	                   TDES1_END_RING : 0;
1216	
1217	      dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1218	                         (uintptr_t)desc +
1219	                         sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1220	
1221	      priv->tx_dirty = (priv->tx_dirty + 1) & (TX_RING_SIZE - 1);
1222	    }
1223	
1224	  up_irq_restore(flags);
1225	}

1227	/****************************************************************************
1228	 * Private Functions — Interrupt Service Routine
1229	 *
1230	 * Reads DMA_STATUS to determine interrupt cause and dispatches accordingly.
1231	 * All DMA status bits are write-1-to-clear.
1232	 *
1233	 * Reference: Manual §7, §10.6
1234	 ****************************************************************************/
1235	
1236	static int sg2000_eth_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
1237	{
1238	  struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv = (struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *)arg;
1239	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
1240	  uint32_t status;
1241	  uint32_t mac_status;
1242	
1243	  /* Read and clear MAC interrupts (if any) */
1244	
1245	  mac_status = getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_INT_STATUS);
1246	  if (mac_status)
1247	    {
1248	      putreg32(mac_status, gmac_base + GMAC_INT_STATUS);
1249	    }
1250	
1251	  /* Read DMA status masked by enabled interrupts */
1252	
1253	  status = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_STATUS) &
1254	           getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_INTR_ENA);
1255	
1256	  if (!status)
1257	    {
1258	      return OK;
1259	    }
1260	
1261	  /* Write-1-to-clear the status bits */
1262	
1263	  putreg32(status & DMA_STATUS_W1C_MASK, gmac_base + DMA_STATUS);
1264	
1265	  /* Handle normal interrupts */
1266	
1267	  if (status & DMA_STATUS_NIS)
1268	    {
1269	      /* Receive interrupt: notify upper half */
1270	
1271	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_RI)
1272	        {
1273	          netdev_lower_rxready(&priv->dev);
1274	        }
1275	
1276	      /* Transmit complete: clean up descriptors */
1277	
1278	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_TI)
1279	        {
1280	          tx_cleanup(priv);
1281	        }
1282	    }
1283	
1284	  /* Handle abnormal interrupts */
1285	
1286	  if (status & DMA_STATUS_AIS)
1287	    {
1288	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_FBI)
1289	        {
1290	          etherr("Fatal Bus Error! bus_mode=0x%08" PRIX32
1291	                 " dma_status=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
1292	                 getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_BUS_MODE), status);
1293	        }
1294	
1295	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_TU)
1296	        {
1297	          ethwarn("TX Buffer Unavailable\n");
1298	        }
1299	
1300	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_RU)
1301	        {
1302	          ethwarn("RX Buffer Unavailable\n");
1303	        }
1304	
1305	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_TPS)
1306	        {
1307	          ethwarn("TX Process Stopped\n");
1308	        }
1309	
1310	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_RPS)
1311	        {
1312	          ethwarn("RX Process Stopped\n");
1313	        }
1314	
1315	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_OVF)
1316	        {
1317	          ethwarn("RX Overflow\n");
1318	        }
1319	
1320	      if (status & DMA_STATUS_UNF)
1321	        {
1322	          ethwarn("TX Underflow\n");
1323	        }
1324	    }
1325	
1326	  return OK;
1327	}

1329	/****************************************************************************
1330	 * Name: netdriver_ifup
1331	 *
1332	 * Description:
1333	 *   OpenVela netdev_ops_s ifup callback.  Performs the full hardware
1334	 *   initialization sequence and brings the interface online.
1335	 *
1336	 * Reference: Manual §4.3, §10.3, §10.11
1337	 ****************************************************************************/
1338	
1339	static int netdriver_ifup(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
1340	{
1341	  FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv =
1342	      (FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *)dev;
1343	  int ret;
1344	
1345	  ethinfo("ifup begin\n");
1346	
1347	  /* 1. Enable clocks and deassert resets */
1348	
1349	  gmac_clock_enable();
1350	
1351	  /* 2. Set GMAC_CORE_INIT (includes PS=MII mode) before PHY operations */
1352	
1353	  putreg32(GMAC_CORE_INIT, priv->gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
1354	
1355	  /* 3. Initialize EPHY via APB */
1356	
1357	  ephy_hardware_reset(priv->phy_base, priv->phy_top);
1358	
1359	  /* 4. Verify MDIO communication with PHY */
1360	
1361	  ret = mdio_verify_phy(priv->gmac_base);
1362	  if (ret < 0)
1363	    {
1364	      etherr("PHY not responding: %d\n", ret);
1365	      return ret;
1366	    }
1367	
1368	  ethinfo("MDIO operational, mdio_addr=0x%08" PRIX32
1369	          " mdio_data=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n",
1370	          getreg32(priv->gmac_base + GMAC_MII_ADDR),
1371	          getreg32(priv->gmac_base + GMAC_MII_DATA));
1372	
1373	  /* 5. Run EPHY full analog tuning (requires operational MDIO) */
1374	
1375	  ephy_full_tuning(priv->phy_base, priv->phy_top);
1376	
1377	  /* 6. Allocate DMA resources (once) */
1378	
1379	  ret = alloc_dma(priv);
1380	  if (ret < 0)
1381	    {
1382	      etherr("alloc_dma failed: %d\n", ret);
1383	      return ret;
1384	    }
1385	
1386	  /* 7. Initialize descriptor rings */
1387	
1388	  init_desc_rings(priv);
1389	
1390	  /* 8. Set MAC address */
1391	
1392	  set_mac_addr(priv->gmac_base, priv->mac_addr);
1393	
1394	  /* 9. Configure PHY (auto-negotiation) BEFORE starting DMA.
1395	   *    Starting DMA while the PHY is in reset causes the TX path to
1396	   *    stall (frames held in FIFO with no RMII link) and the RX path
1397	   *    to pick up garbage from an unstable RMII interface.
1398	   */
1399	
1400	  ret = phy_config_init(priv);
1401	  if (ret < 0)
1402	    {
1403	      etherr("PHY config failed: %d\n", ret);
1404	      return ret;
1405	    }
1406	
1407	  /* Apply negotiated speed/duplex to GMAC before DMA start */
1408	
1409	  gmac_set_speed_duplex(priv->gmac_base, priv->speed, priv->duplex);
1410	
1411	  /* 10. Hardware setup: DMA reset, MAC core, DMA mode, start DMA.
1412	   *    Performed AFTER PHY is ready — clean RMII link and stable speed.
1413	   */
1414	
1415	  ret = hw_setup(priv);
1416	  if (ret < 0)
1417	    {
1418	      etherr("hw_setup failed: %d\n", ret);
1419	      return ret;
1420	    }
1421	
1422	  /* 11. Ring RX doorbell and enable interrupts (last, after all HW init) */
1423	
1424	  rx_doorbell(priv->gmac_base);
1425	  up_enable_irq(priv->irq);
1426	
1427	  /* 12. Signal carrier on to the network stack (if link detected) */
1428	
1429	  if (priv->link_up)
1430	    {
1431	      netdev_lower_carrier_on(dev);
1432	    }
1433	
1434	  ethinfo("ifup done: %d Mbps %s duplex, link=%s\n",
1435	          priv->speed, priv->duplex ? "Full" : "Half",
1436	          priv->link_up ? "up" : "down");
1437	
1438	  return OK;
1439	}

1441	/****************************************************************************
1442	 * Name: netdriver_ifdown
1443	 *
1444	 * Description:
1445	 *   OpenVela netdev_ops_s ifdown callback.  Stops DMA, disables MAC,
1446	 *   and disables interrupts.
1447	 *
1448	 * Reference: Manual §4.3
1449	 ****************************************************************************/
1450	
1451	static int netdriver_ifdown(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
1452	{
1453	  FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv =
1454	      (FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *)dev;
1455	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
1456	  uint32_t val;
1457	
1458	  up_disable_irq(priv->irq);
1459	
1460	  /* Stop TX and RX DMA */
1461	
1462	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1463	  putreg32(val & ~(DMA_CONTROL_ST | DMA_CONTROL_SR), gmac_base + DMA_CONTROL);
1464	
1465	  /* Disable MAC TX/RX */
1466	
1467	  val = getreg32(gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
1468	  putreg32(val & ~(GMAC_CONTROL_TE | GMAC_CONTROL_RE),
1469	           gmac_base + GMAC_CONTROL);
1470	
1471	  /* Disable DMA interrupts */
1472	
1473	  putreg32(0, gmac_base + DMA_INTR_ENA);
1474	
1475	  /* Clear pending interrupts */
1476	
1477	  putreg32(DMA_STATUS_W1C_MASK, gmac_base + DMA_STATUS);
1478	
1479	  netdev_lower_carrier_off(dev);
1480	
1481	  priv->link_up = 0;
1482	
1483	  ethinfo("ifdown: interface stopped\n");
1484	
1485	  return OK;
1486	}

1488	/****************************************************************************
1489	 * Name: netdriver_transmit
1490	 *
1491	 * Description:
1492	 *   OpenVela netdev_ops_s transmit callback.  Sends a packet via DMA.
1493	 *   The driver takes ownership of the netpkt and MUST free it after
1494	 *   TX completion (in tx_cleanup) or on error.
1495	 *
1496	 * Reference: Manual §5.1, §10.4
1497	 ****************************************************************************/
1498	
1499	static int netdriver_transmit(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev,
1500	                               FAR netpkt_t *pkt)
1501	{
1502	  FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv =
1503	      (FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *)dev;
1504	  unsigned int len = netpkt_getdatalen(dev, pkt);
1505	  uint8_t tmp_buf[SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE];
1506	  const uint8_t *data;
1507	  irqstate_t flags;
1508	  int ret;
1509	
1510	  if (len > SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE)
1511	    {
1512	      etherr("TX packet too large: %u\n", len);
1513	      return -E2BIG;
1514	    }
1515	
1516	  /* Extract data from netpkt.  If fragmented, copy to tmp_buf;
1517	   * otherwise use pointer directly.
1518	   */
1519	
1520	  if (netpkt_is_fragmented(pkt))
1521	    {
1522	      netpkt_copyout(dev, tmp_buf, pkt, len, 0);
1523	      data = tmp_buf;
1524	    }
1525	  else
1526	    {
1527	      data = netpkt_getdata(dev, pkt);
1528	      if (!data)
1529	        {
1530	          etherr("netpkt_getdata returned NULL\n");
1531	          return -EINVAL;
1532	        }
1533	    }
1534	
1535	  /* Transmit via DMA.  Track the netpkt BEFORE calling hw_transmit
1536	   * (which advances tx_cur) so the ISR can't observe a half-committed
1537	   * slot.  The whole section runs with IRQs off to close the race
1538	   * between pkt store, cur advance, and ISR tx_cleanup.
1539	   *
1540	   * On failure, do NOT free the netpkt — the upper half recycles it.
1541	   */
1542	
1543	  flags = up_irq_save();
1544	  priv->tx_pkt[priv->tx_cur] = pkt;
1545	
1546	  ret = hw_transmit(priv, data, len);
1547	  if (ret < 0)
1548	    {
1549	      priv->tx_pkt[priv->tx_cur] = NULL;  /* Undo — slot not consumed */
1550	      up_irq_restore(flags);
1551	      etherr("hw_transmit failed: %d\n", ret);
1552	      return ret;
1553	    }
1554	
1555	  up_irq_restore(flags);
1556	
1557	  return OK;
1558	}

1560	/****************************************************************************
1561	 * Name: netdriver_receive
1562	 *
1563	 * Description:
1564	 *   OpenVela netdev_ops_s receive callback.  Called by upper half when
1565	 *   netdev_lower_rxready() was signaled.  Returns one received packet,
1566	 *   or NULL if no more packets are available.
1567	 *
1568	 * Reference: Manual §6, §10.5
1569	 ****************************************************************************/
1570	
1571	static FAR netpkt_t *netdriver_receive(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
1572	{
1573	  FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv =
1574	      (FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *)dev;
1575	  FAR netpkt_t *pkt = NULL;
1576	  struct sg2000_dma_desc_s *desc;
1577	  uintptr_t gmac_base = priv->gmac_base;
1578	  uint32_t status;
1579	  int frame_len;
1580	  int ret;
1581	
1582	  desc = &priv->rx_desc[priv->rx_cur];
1583	
1584	  /* Invalidate descriptor cache line to read DMA-written status */
1585	
1586	  dcache_invalidate_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1587	                          (uintptr_t)desc +
1588	                          sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1589	
1590	  /* Check if DMA still owns the descriptor (no packet ready) */
1591	
1592	  if (desc->des0 & RDES0_OWN)
1593	    {
1594	      return NULL;
1595	    }
1596	
1597	  status = desc->des0;
1598	
1599	  /* Check for receive errors */
1600	
1601	  if (status & RDES0_ERROR_SUMMARY)
1602	    {
1603	      etherr("RX error status=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n", status);
1604	      goto refill;
1605	    }
1606	
1607	  /* Verify we got a complete frame (first AND last descriptor) */
1608	
1609	  if (!(status & RDES0_FIRST_DESCRIPTOR) ||
1610	      !(status & RDES0_LAST_DESCRIPTOR))
1611	    {
1612	      ethwarn("RX incomplete frame, status=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n", status);
1613	      goto refill;
1614	    }
1615	
1616	  /* Get frame length (includes 4-byte FCS which we strip) */
1617	
1618	  frame_len = (int)((status & RDES0_FRAME_LEN_MASK) >> RDES0_FRAME_LEN_SHIFT)
1619	              - ETH_FCSSLEN;
1620	
1621	  if (frame_len <= 0 || frame_len > CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE)
1622	    {
1623	      ethwarn("RX invalid frame length: %d\n", frame_len);
1624	      goto refill;
1625	    }
1626	
1627	  /* Invalidate RX data buffer to read DMA-written data */
1628	
1629	  dcache_invalidate_range((uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[priv->rx_cur],
1630	                          (uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[priv->rx_cur] +
1631	                          RX_BUF_SIZE);
1632	
1633	  /* Allocate a netpkt for the received data */
1634	
1635	  pkt = netpkt_alloc(dev, NETPKT_RX);
1636	  if (!pkt)
1637	    {
1638	      etherr("netpkt_alloc failed\n");
1639	      goto refill;
1640	    }
1641	
1642	  /* Copy data from DMA buffer into netpkt */
1643	
1644	  ret = netpkt_copyin(dev, pkt, priv->rx_buf[priv->rx_cur], frame_len, 0);
1645	  if (ret < 0)
1646	    {
1647	      etherr("netpkt_copyin failed: %d\n", ret);
1648	      netpkt_free(dev, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
1649	      pkt = NULL;
1650	      goto refill;
1651	    }
1652	
1653	  ethinfo("RX: %d bytes desc[%u]\n", frame_len, priv->rx_cur);
1654	
1655	refill:
1656	  /* Return descriptor to DMA: set OWN=1, restore buffer address.
1657	   * Preserve END_RING bit for the last descriptor in des1.
1658	   */
1659	
1660	  desc->des0 = RDES0_OWN;
1661	  desc->des1 = (RX_BUF_SIZE & RDES1_BUFFER1_SIZE_MASK) |
1662	               ((priv->rx_cur == (RX_RING_SIZE - 1)) ? RDES1_END_RING : 0);
1663	  desc->des2 = priv->rx_buf_phys[priv->rx_cur];
1664	
1665	  /* Flush RX buffer before handing it back to DMA */
1666	
1667	  dcache_flush_range((uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[priv->rx_cur],
1668	                     (uintptr_t)priv->rx_buf[priv->rx_cur] + RX_BUF_SIZE);
1669	
1670	  /* Write back descriptor so DMA sees OWN=1 */
1671	
1672	  dcache_clean_range((uintptr_t)desc,
1673	                     (uintptr_t)desc + sizeof(struct sg2000_dma_desc_s));
1674	
1675	  priv->rx_cur = (priv->rx_cur + 1) & (RX_RING_SIZE - 1);
1676	  rx_doorbell(gmac_base);
1677	
1678	  return pkt;
1679	}

1697	/****************************************************************************
1698	 * Name: sg2000_eth_initialize
1699	 *
1700	 * Description:
1701	 *   Initialize the SG2000 Ethernet driver and register it with the OpenVela
1702	 *   network stack as a netdev_lowerhalf_s device.
1703	 *
1704	 *   Called from board_late_initialize() during system bringup.
1705	 *
1706	 ****************************************************************************/
1707	
1708	int sg2000_eth_initialize(void)
1709	{
1710	  FAR struct sg2000_eth_priv_s *priv = &g_eth_priv;
1711	  FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev = &priv->dev;
1712	  int ret;
1713	
1714	  if (g_eth_initialized)
1715	    {
1716	      return OK;
1717	    }
1718	
1719	  /* Initialize private data */
1720	
1721	  memset(priv, 0, sizeof(*priv));
1722	  priv->gmac_base = SG2000_GMAC_BASE;
1723	  priv->phy_base  = SG2000_EPHY_BASE;
1724	  priv->phy_top   = SG2000_EPHY_TOP;
1725	
1726	  /* Set default MAC address (should be replaced with eFuse/OTP value) */
1727	
1728	  priv->mac_addr[0] = 0x02;
1729	  priv->mac_addr[1] = 0x00;
1730	  priv->mac_addr[2] = 0x00;
1731	  priv->mac_addr[3] = 0x00;
1732	  priv->mac_addr[4] = 0x00;
1733	  priv->mac_addr[5] = 0x01;
1734	
1735	  /* Copy MAC address to the netdev structure */
1736	
1737	  memcpy(dev->netdev.d_mac.ether.ether_addr_octet, priv->mac_addr,
1738	         IFHWADDRLEN);
1739	
1740	  /* Configure device quotas and operations.
1741	   * Total quota (TX + RX) must not exceed CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS.
1742	   * With CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=64, we reserve 16 each (32 total).
1743	   */
1744	
1745	  dev->quota[NETPKT_TX] = 16;
1746	  dev->quota[NETPKT_RX] = 16;
1747	  dev->ops              = &g_ops;
1748	
1749	  /* Get the GMAC interrupt number */
1750	
1751	  priv->irq = SG2000_IRQ_GMAC;
1752	
1753	  /* Register with the OpenVela network stack */
1754	
1755	  ret = netdev_lower_register(dev, NET_LL_ETHERNET);
1756	  if (ret < 0)
1757	    {
1758	      etherr("netdev_lower_register failed: %d\n", ret);
1759	      return ret;
1760	    }
1761	
1762	  /* Initially, carrier is off */
1763	
1764	  netdev_lower_carrier_off(dev);
1765	  g_eth_initialized = true;
1766	
1767	  ethinfo("SG2000 Ethernet driver registered as eth0\n");
1768	
1769	  /* Attach interrupt handler (once).
1770	   * The IRQ is NOT enabled here — it is enabled at the end of
1771	   * netdriver_ifup() only after the hardware is fully configured.
1772	   */
1773	
1774	  ret = irq_attach(priv->irq, sg2000_eth_isr, priv);
1775	  if (ret < 0)
1776	    {
1777	      etherr("irq_attach failed: %d\n", ret);
1778	      return OK;  /* Driver is still registered, just no interrupts */
1779	    }
1780	
1781	  ethinfo("IRQ %d attached (not yet enabled)\n", priv->irq);
1782	
1783	  return OK;
1784	}

55	/* These definitions define the characteristics of the allocator:
56	 *
57	 * MM_MIN_SHIFT is used to define MM_MIN_CHUNK.
58	 * MM_MIN_CHUNK - is the smallest physical chunk that can be allocated.
59	 *   It must be at least as large as sizeof(struct mm_freenode_s). Larger
60	 *   values may improve performance slightly, but will waste memory due to
61	 *   quantization losses.
62	 *
63	 * MM_MAX_SHIFT is used to define MM_MAX_CHUNK
64	 * MM_MAX_CHUNK is the largest, contiguous chunk of memory that can be
65	 *   allocated.  It can range from 16-bytes to 4Gb.  Larger values of
66	 *   MM_MAX_SHIFT can cause larger data structure sizes and, perhaps,
67	 *   minor performance losses.
68	 */
69	
70	#define MM_MIN_SHIFT      LOG2_CEIL(sizeof(struct mm_freenode_s))
71	#if defined(CONFIG_MM_SMALL) && UINTPTR_MAX <= UINT32_MAX
72	#  define MM_MAX_SHIFT    (15)  /* 32 Kb */
73	#else
74	#  define MM_MAX_SHIFT    (22)  /*  4 Mb */
75	#endif
76	
77	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_PID
78	#  define MM_RECORD_PID(node, tid) ((node)->pid = tid)
79	#else
80	#  define MM_RECORD_PID(node, tid)
81	#endif
82	
83	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK
84	#  define MM_RECORD_STACK(node, tid) \
85	    do \
86	      { \
87	        FAR struct tls_info_s *info = tls_get_info(); \
88	        if (((heap)->mm_procfs && (heap)->mm_procfs->backtrace) || \
89	            (info && info->tl_flags & TLS_FLAG_HEAP_DUMP)) \
90	          { \
91	            (node)->stack = backtrace_record(CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK_SKIP); \
92	          } \
93	        else \
94	          { \
95	            (node)->stack = NULL; \
96	          } \
97	      } \
98	    while (0)
99	#else
100	#  define MM_RECORD_STACK(node, tid)
101	#endif
102	
103	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD
104	#  define MM_RECORD(heap, ptr) \
105	     do \
106	       { \
107	         FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *tmp = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)(ptr); \
108	         pid_t tid = _SCHED_GETTID(); \
109	         UNUSED(tid); \
110	         MM_INCSEQNO(tmp); \
111	         MM_RECORD_PID(tmp, tid); \
112	         MM_RECORD_STACK(tmp, tid); \
113	       } \
114	     while (0)
115	#else
116	#  define MM_RECORD(heap, ptr)
117	#endif
118	
119	/* All other definitions derive from these two */
120	
121	#define MM_MIN_CHUNK     (1 << MM_MIN_SHIFT)
122	#define MM_MAX_CHUNK     (1 << MM_MAX_SHIFT)
123	#define MM_NNODES        (MM_MAX_SHIFT - MM_MIN_SHIFT + 1)
124	
125	#define MM_GRAN_MASK     (MM_ALIGN - 1)
126	#define MM_ALIGN_UP(a)   (((a) + MM_GRAN_MASK) & ~MM_GRAN_MASK)
127	#define MM_ALIGN_DOWN(a) ((a) & ~MM_GRAN_MASK)
128	
129	/* Due to alignment, the lowest two bits of valid chunk size are always
130	 * zero, thus the two bits are reused to depict allocation status: bit
131	 * 0 depicts the allocation state of current chunk, and bit 1 depicts that
132	 * of the physically preceding chunk.
133	 */
134	
135	#define MM_ALLOC_BIT     0x1
136	#define MM_PREVFREE_BIT  0x2
137	#define MM_MASK_BIT      (MM_ALLOC_BIT | MM_PREVFREE_BIT)
138	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_SMALL
139	#  define MMSIZE_MAX     UINT16_MAX
140	#else
141	#  define MMSIZE_MAX     UINT32_MAX
142	#endif
143	
144	/* What is the size of the allocnode? */
145	
146	#define MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE sizeof(struct mm_allocnode_s)
147	
148	/* What is the overhead of the allocnode
149	 * Remove the space of preceding field since it locates at the end of the
150	 * previous freenode
151	 */
152	
153	#define MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD (CONFIG_MM_NODE_GUARDSIZE + \
154	                               MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE - sizeof(mmsize_t))
155	
156	/* Get the node size */
157	
158	#define MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node) ((node)->size & (~MM_MASK_BIT))
159	
160	/* Check if node/prenode is free */
161	
162	#define MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node) (((node)->size & MM_ALLOC_BIT) != 0)
163	#define MM_NODE_IS_FREE(node) (((node)->size & MM_ALLOC_BIT) == 0)
164	
165	#define MM_PREVNODE_IS_ALLOC(node) (((node)->size & MM_PREVFREE_BIT) == 0)
166	#define MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node) (((node)->size & MM_PREVFREE_BIT) != 0)

334	static inline_function int mm_size2ndx(size_t size)
335	{
336	  DEBUGASSERT(size >= MM_MIN_CHUNK);
337	  if (size >= MM_MAX_CHUNK)
338	    {
339	      return MM_NNODES - 1;
340	    }
341	
342	  size >>= MM_MIN_SHIFT;
343	  return flsl(size) - 1;
344	}
345	
346	static inline_function void mm_addfreechunk(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap,
347	                                            FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node)
348	{
349	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
350	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev;
351	  size_t nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
352	  int ndx;
353	
354	  DEBUGASSERT(nodesize >= MM_MIN_CHUNK);
355	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_FREE(node));
356	
357	  /* Convert the size to a nodelist index */
358	
359	  ndx = mm_size2ndx(nodesize);
360	
361	  /* Now put the new node into the next */
362	
363	  for (prev = &heap->mm_nodelist[ndx],
364	       next = heap->mm_nodelist[ndx].flink;
365	       next && next->size && MM_SIZEOF_NODE(next) < nodesize;
366	       prev = next, next = next->flink);
367	
368	  /* Does it go in mid next or at the end? */
369	
370	  prev->flink = node;
371	  node->blink = prev;
372	  node->flink = next;
373	
374	  if (next)
375	    {
376	      /* The new node goes between prev and next */
377	
378	      next->blink = node;
379	    }
380	}

143	/* CSR clock divider value for MDC ≈ 1MHz:
144	 * CSR_CLK = 250MHz, desired MDC = 1~2.5MHz
145	 * MDC = CSR_CLK / (2 * (csr_div + 1)) where csr_div is 0-63
146	 * For 1MHz: csr_div = 124, but max is 63, so use 124 via CR field
147	 * With CR=5 (div 10): MDC = 250/20 = 12.5MHz — high but works
148	 * For proper 1MHz use csr_div=124 direct:
149	 *   MDC = 250 / (2 * (124+1)) = 250/250 = 1MHz
150	 * But the hardware max for CR field is only 0-63.
151	 * With max CR=63: MDC = 250/(2*63) ≈ 2MHz (acceptable range)
152	 * Linux uses the CR field where CR selects from a lookup table,
153	 * use the same value as the Linux driver: CR=5 (matches dwmac-cvitek.c)
154	 */

157	 * use value 124 for ~1MHz MDC from 250MHz CSR clock

46	static void add_delaylist(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem,
47	                          bool asan_check)
48	{
49	#if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__)
50	  FAR struct mm_delayhead_s *delay = get_delayhead(heap);
51	  FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *tmp = mem;
52	  irqstate_t flags;
53	  bool bypass;
54	
55	  /* Delay the deallocation until a more appropriate time. */
56	
57	  flags = up_irq_save();
58	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
59	
60	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS
61	  /* Check for double-free:
62	   * Step 1: Check magic first (fast path, filters 99.99% cases)
63	   * Step 2: If magic matches, verify it's actually in delay list
64	   *         (slow path, handles extreme case where user data == magic)
65	   */
66	
67	  if (tmp->magic == ~(uintptr_t)mem)
68	    {
69	      /* Magic matches, but could be false positive from user data.
70	       * Traverse delay list to confirm this is really a duplicate.
71	       */
72	
73	      FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *node;
74	
75	      for (node = delay->head; node != NULL; node = node->flink)
76	        {
77	          if (node == tmp)
78	            {
79	              /* Confirmed: this memory is already in delay list.
80	               * This is a real double-free!
81	               */
82	
83	              kasan_bypass(bypass);
84	              up_irq_restore(flags);
85	              DEBUGASSERT(false);  /* Double-free detected! */
86	              return;
87	            }
88	        }
89	
90	      /* Magic matched but not in list - just user data coincidence.
91	       * Continue with normal flow.
92	       */
93	    }
94	
95	#  ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
96	  if (!heap->mm_mpool || !mempool_multiple_member(heap->mm_mpool, mem))
97	#  endif
98	    {
99	      FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
100	      node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)mem -
101	             MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
102	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
103	    }
104	
105	  tmp->magic = ~(uintptr_t)mem;
106	#endif
107	
108	  tmp->flink  = delay->head;
109	  delay->head = tmp;
110	
111	#if CONFIG_MM_FREE_DELAYCOUNT_MAX > 0
112	  delay->delaycount++;
113	#endif
114	
115	  if (asan_check)
116	    {
117	      size_t size = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
118	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
119	      memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, size);
120	#endif
121	      UNUSED(size);
122	      kasan_poison(mem, size);
123	    }
124	
125	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
126	  up_irq_restore(flags);
127	#endif
128	}

142	void mm_forcefree(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem)
143	{
144	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
145	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev;
146	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
147	  size_t nodesize;
148	  size_t prevsize;
149	  bool bypass;
150	
151	  /* Free mempool blk first */
152	
153	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
154	  if (heap->mm_mpool && mempool_multiple_free(heap->mm_mpool, mem) >= 0)
155	    {
156	      return;
157	    }
158	#endif
159	
160	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
161	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
162	  nodesize = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
163	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
164	  memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, nodesize);
165	#endif
166	  kasan_poison(mem, nodesize);
167	
168	  /* Map the memory chunk into a free node */
169	
170	  node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
171	         ((FAR char *)kasan_clear_tag(mem) - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
172	  nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
173	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK
174	  backtrace_remove(node->stack);
175	#endif
176	
177	  /* Sanity check against double-frees */
178	
179	  if (MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node))
180	    {
181	      mm_trace_diag(DIAG_MM_FREE_FAIL, "address:%p, reason:%s",
182	                    mem, "double-free");
183	    }
184	
185	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
186	  node->size &= ~MM_ALLOC_BIT;
187	
188	  /* Update heap statistics */
189	
190	  heap->mm_curused -= nodesize;
191	  sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_FREE, heap, mem, nodesize, heap->mm_curused);
192	
193	  /* Check if the following node is free and, if so, merge it */
194	
195	  next = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node + nodesize);
196	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_ALLOC(next));
197	  if (MM_NODE_IS_FREE(next))
198	    {
199	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *andbeyond;
200	      size_t nextsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(next);
201	
202	      /* Get the node following the next node (which will
203	       * become the new next node). We know that we can never
204	       * index past the tail chunk because it is always allocated.
205	       */
206	
207	      andbeyond = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)((FAR char *)next + nextsize);
208	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(andbeyond) &&
209	                  andbeyond->preceding == nextsize);
210	
211	      /* Remove the next node.  There must be a predecessor,
212	       * but there may not be a successor node.
213	       */
214	
215	      DEBUGASSERT(next->blink);
216	      next->blink->flink = next->flink;
217	      if (next->flink)
218	        {
219	          next->flink->blink = next->blink;
220	        }
221	
222	      /* Then merge the two chunks */
223	
224	      nodesize            += nextsize;
225	      node->size           = nodesize | (node->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
226	      andbeyond->preceding = nodesize;
227	      next                 = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)andbeyond;
228	    }
229	  else
230	    {
231	      next->size     |= MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
232	      next->preceding = nodesize;
233	    }
234	
235	  /* Check if the preceding node is also free and, if so, merge
236	   * it with this node
237	   */
238	
239	  if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
240	    {
241	      prev = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
242	        ((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
243	      prevsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
244	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_FREE(prev) && node->preceding == prevsize);
245	
246	      /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
247	       * not be a successor node.
248	       */
249	
250	      DEBUGASSERT(prev->blink);
251	      prev->blink->flink = prev->flink;
252	      if (prev->flink)
253	        {
254	          prev->flink->blink = prev->blink;
255	        }
256	
257	      /* Then merge the two chunks */
258	
259	      prevsize       += nodesize;
260	      prev->size      = prevsize | (prev->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
261	      next->preceding = prevsize;
262	      node            = prev;
263	    }
264	
265	  /* Add the merged node to the nodelist */
266	
267	  mm_addfreechunk(heap, node);
268	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
269	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
270	}

42	/****************************************************************************
43	 * Name: mm_memalign
44	 *
45	 * Description:
46	 *   memalign requests more than enough space from malloc, finds a region
47	 *   within that chunk that meets the alignment request and then frees any
48	 *   leading or trailing space.
49	 *
50	 *   The alignment argument must be a power of two. 16-byte alignment is
51	 *   guaranteed by normal malloc calls.
52	 *
53	 ****************************************************************************/
54	
55	FAR void *mm_memalign(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, size_t alignment,
56	                      size_t size)
57	{
58	  FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *node;
59	  uintptr_t rawchunk;
60	  uintptr_t alignedchunk;
61	  size_t mask;
62	  size_t allocsize;
63	  size_t newsize;
64	  bool bypass;
65	
66	  /* Make sure that alignment is less than half max size_t */
67	
68	  if (alignment >= (SIZE_MAX / 2))
69	    {
70	      return NULL;
71	    }
72	
73	  /* Make sure that alignment is a power of 2 */
74	
75	  if ((alignment & -alignment) != alignment)
76	    {
77	      return NULL;
78	    }
79	
80	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
81	  if (heap->mm_mpool)
82	    {
83	      node = mempool_multiple_memalign(heap->mm_mpool, alignment, size);
84	      if (node != NULL)
85	        {
86	          return node;
87	        }
88	    }
89	#endif
90	
91	  /* If this requested alinement's less than or equal to the natural
92	   * alignment of malloc, then just let malloc do the work.
93	   */
94	
95	  if (alignment <= MM_ALIGN)
96	    {
97	      FAR void *ptr = mm_malloc(heap, size);
98	      DEBUGASSERT(ptr == NULL || ((uintptr_t)ptr) % alignment == 0);
99	      return ptr;
100	    }
101	  else if (alignment < MM_MIN_CHUNK)
102	    {
103	      alignment = MM_MIN_CHUNK;
104	    }
105	
106	  mask = alignment - 1;
107	
108	  /* Adjust the size to account for (1) the size of the allocated node and
109	   * (2) to make sure that it is aligned with MM_ALIGN and its size is at
110	   * least MM_MIN_CHUNK.
111	   *
112	   * Notice that we increase the allocation size by twice the requested
113	   * alignment.  We do this so that there will be at least two valid
114	   * alignment points within the allocated memory.
115	   *
116	   * NOTE:  These are sizes given to malloc and not chunk sizes. They do
117	   * not include MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE.
118	   */
119	
120	  if (size < MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD)
121	    {
122	      size = MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD;
123	    }
124	
125	  newsize = MM_ALIGN_UP(size);         /* Make multiples of our granule size */
126	  allocsize = newsize + 2 * alignment; /* Add double full alignment size */
127	
128	  if (newsize < size || allocsize < newsize)
129	    {
130	      /* Integer overflow */
131	
132	      return NULL;
133	    }
134	
135	  /* Then malloc that size */
136	
137	  rawchunk = (uintptr_t)mm_malloc(heap, allocsize);
138	  if (rawchunk == 0)
139	    {
140	      return NULL;
141	    }
142	
143	  kasan_poison((FAR void *)rawchunk,
144	               mm_malloc_size(heap, (FAR void *)rawchunk));
145	
146	  rawchunk = (uintptr_t)kasan_clear_tag((FAR void *)rawchunk);
147	
148	  /* We need to hold the MM mutex while we muck with the chunks and
149	   * nodelist.
150	   */
151	
152	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
153	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
154	
155	  /* Get the node associated with the allocation and the next node after
156	   * the allocation.
157	   */
158	
159	  node = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)(rawchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
160	  heap->mm_curused -= MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
161	
162	  /* Find the aligned subregion */
163	
164	  alignedchunk = (rawchunk + mask) & ~mask;
165	
166	  /* Check if there is free space at the beginning of the aligned chunk */
167	
168	  if (alignedchunk != rawchunk)
169	    {
170	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *newnode;
171	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *next;
172	      size_t precedingsize;
173	      size_t newnodesize;
174	
175	      /* Get the node the next node after the allocation. */
176	
177	      next = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
178	        ((FAR char *)node + MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node));
179	
180	      newnode = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
181	        (alignedchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
182	
183	      /* Preceding size is full size of the new 'node,' including
184	       * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE
185	       */
186	
187	      precedingsize = (uintptr_t)newnode - (uintptr_t)node;
188	
189	      /* If we were unlucky, then the alignedchunk can lie in such a position
190	       * that precedingsize < SIZEOF_NODE_FREENODE.  We can't let that happen
191	       * because we are going to cast 'node' to struct mm_freenode_s below.
192	       * This is why we allocated memory large enough to support two
193	       * alignment points.  In this case, we will simply use the second
194	       * alignment point.
195	       */
196	
197	      if (precedingsize < MM_MIN_CHUNK)
198	        {
199	          alignedchunk += alignment;
200	          newnode       = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
201	                          (alignedchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
202	          precedingsize = (uintptr_t)newnode - (uintptr_t)node;
203	        }
204	
205	      /* If the previous node is free, merge node and previous node, then
206	       * set up the node size.
207	       */
208	
209	      if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
210	        {
211	          FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev =
212	            (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
213	
214	          /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
215	           * not be a successor node.
216	           */
217	
218	          DEBUGASSERT(prev->blink);
219	          prev->blink->flink = prev->flink;
220	          if (prev->flink)
221	            {
222	              prev->flink->blink = prev->blink;
223	            }
224	
225	          precedingsize += MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
226	          node = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)prev;
227	        }
228	
229	      node->size = precedingsize;
230	
231	      /* Set up the size of the new node */
232	
233	      newnodesize = (uintptr_t)next - (uintptr_t)newnode;
234	      newnode->size = newnodesize | MM_ALLOC_BIT | MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
235	      newnode->preceding = precedingsize;
236	
237	      /* Clear the previous free bit of the next node */
238	
239	      next->size &= ~MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
240	
241	      /* Convert the newnode chunk size back into malloc-compatible size by
242	       * subtracting the header size MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD.
243	       */
244	
245	      allocsize = newnodesize - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD;
246	
247	      /* Add the original, newly freed node to the free nodelist */
248	
249	      mm_addfreechunk(heap, (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)node);
250	
251	      /* Replace the original node with the newlay realloaced,
252	       * aligned node
253	       */
254	
255	      node = newnode;
256	    }
257	
258	  /* Check if there is free space at the end of the aligned chunk. Convert
259	   * malloc-compatible chunk size to include MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD as needed
260	   * for mm_shrinkchunk.
261	   */
262	
263	  size = MM_ALIGN_UP(size + MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD);
264	
265	  if (allocsize > size)
266	    {
267	      /* Shrink the chunk by that much -- remember, mm_shrinkchunk wants
268	       * internal chunk sizes that include MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD.
269	       */
270	
271	      mm_shrinkchunk(heap, node, size);
272	    }
273	
274	  /* Update heap statistics */
275	
276	  size = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
277	  heap->mm_curused += size;
278	  if (heap->mm_curused > heap->mm_maxused)
279	    {
280	      heap->mm_maxused = heap->mm_curused;
281	    }
282	
283	  sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_ALLOC, heap, (FAR void *)alignedchunk, size,
284	                  heap->mm_curused);
285	
286	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
287	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
288	
289	  MM_RECORD(heap, node);
290	
291	  alignedchunk = (uintptr_t)kasan_unpoison((FAR const void *)alignedchunk,
292	                                           size - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD);
293	  DEBUGASSERT(alignedchunk % alignment == 0);
294	  minfo("Aligned %"PRIxPTR" to %"PRIxPTR", size %zu\n",
295	        rawchunk, alignedchunk, size);
296	  return (FAR void *)alignedchunk;
297	}

708	static void netdev_upper_rxpoll_work(FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper)
709	{

711	  FAR struct net_driver_s       *dev   = &lower->netdev;
712	  FAR netpkt_t                  *pkt;
713	
714	  /* Loop while receive() successfully retrieves valid Ethernet frames. */
715	
716	  netdev_lock(dev);
717	  while ((pkt = lower->ops->receive(lower)) != NULL)
718	    {
719	      if (!IFF_IS_UP(dev->d_flags))
720	        {
721	          /* Interface down, drop frame */
722	
723	          NETDEV_RXDROPPED(dev);
724	          netpkt_free(lower, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
725	          nerr("ERROR: Dropped frame due to lower dev not up\n");
726	          continue;
727	        }
728	
729	      netpkt_put(dev, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
730	      NETDEV_RXPACKETS(dev);
731	
732	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
733	      /* When packet sockets are enabled, feed the frame into the tap */
734

742	#endif
743	#ifdef CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET

172	/****************************************************************************
173	 * Private Functions — D-Cache Operations (T-Head C906)
174	 *
175	 * The C906 has a 32KB 4-way set-associative D-Cache with 64-byte cache
176	 * lines using PIPT (Physical Index + Physical Tag).  DDR memory
177	 * (0x80000000-0xC0000000) is mapped as cacheable.  DMA descriptors and
178	 * buffers allocated from the kernel heap are therefore cacheable, and
179	 * explicit cache maintenance is REQUIRED before any DMA engine access.
180	 *
181	 * The Synopsys DWMAC1000 DMA engine is NOT cache-coherent on this SoC.
182	 *
183	 * T-Head custom instructions (from CV181x/SG2002 TRM):
184	 *   dcache.cpa  rs1  (0x0295000b)  – Clean (write back) by physical addr
185	 *   dcache.ipa  rs1  (0x02a5000b)  – Invalidate by physical addr
186	 *   dcache.cipa rs1  (0x02b5000b)  – Clean + Invalidate by physical addr
187	 *   sync.s           (0x01b0000b)  – Cache operation sync barrier
188	 ****************************************************************************/
189	
190	static void dcache_clean_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
191	{
192	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
193	
194	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
195	    {
196	      asm volatile (".long 0x0295000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.cpa a0 */
197	    }
198	
199	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
200	}
201	
202	static void dcache_invalidate_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
203	{
204	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
205	
206	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
207	    {
208	      asm volatile (".long 0x02a5000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.ipa a0 */
209	    }
210	
211	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
212	}
213	
214	static void dcache_flush_range(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
215	{
216	  register uintptr_t i asm("a0") = start & ~(C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE - 1);
217	
218	  for (; i < end; i += C906_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
219	    {
220	      asm volatile (".long 0x02b5000b" ::: "memory");  /* dcache.cipa a0 */
221	    }
222	
223	  asm volatile (".long 0x01b0000b" ::: "memory");      /* sync.s */
224	}
